title: Profiling with Tachyon
description: Guided JupyterLab workshops on Tachyon, the sampling profiler in Python 3.15: what a sample is and why sampling costs nothing, reading the table, the flame graph and the heatmap, choosing wall, CPU, GIL or exception time, threads, async code, native code and the garbage collector, bytecode, comparing two profiles, and watching a program live.

workshops.name: your-first-profile
workshops.title: Your first profile
workshops.description: Run Tachyon, the sampling profiler in Python 3.15, on a small report generator and read the table it prints. Learn what a sample is, why time is samples multiplied by an interval, why the same function can fill two rows, and which of the report's functions is eating the time.

workshops.name: sampling-or-tracing
workshops.title: Sampling or tracing?
workshops.description: Run the same report under cProfile, now also called profiling.tracing, and under Tachyon. Exact call counts against estimates, the overhead each imposes and why it depends on how many calls a program makes, and which profiler to reach for when.

workshops.name: reading-a-process-from-outside
workshops.title: Reading a process from the outside
workshops.description: How Tachyon sees the call stack of another process without running any code in it, why that needs permission on most systems, why the profiler and the program must be the same Python, and what the error rate and the blocking option mean.

workshops.name: reading-a-flame-graph
workshops.title: Reading a flame graph
workshops.description: Turn a Tachyon profile into the interactive flame graph the profiler writes and read it beside the instructions, on a page renderer whose hot function has several callers. What width and depth mean, zooming, search, the sidebar, and the collapsed stacks text the picture is drawn from.

workshops.name: down-to-the-line
workshops.title: Down to the line
workshops.description: Paint a Tachyon profile onto the source code with the heatmap, on a report whose slow function is twenty lines long and slow on one of them. The index of files, the page per file, self and total time, the hot-only filter, and the same file before and after the fix.

workshops.name: record-now-look-later
workshops.title: Record now, look later
workshops.description: Record a Tachyon profile once in the compact binary format and turn it into a table, a flame graph and a heatmap afterwards with replay. Then the formats for other tools, the gecko file the Firefox Profiler reads, JSONL for your own scripts and the pstats file, and what each output is for.

workshops.name: waiting-or-working
workshops.title: Waiting or working?
workshops.description: Find out whether a slow program is computing or waiting, with Tachyon's wall-clock and CPU modes, on a feed reader that fetches from a slow server and then merges what it fetched. What each mode keeps, why the two tables disagree, and what the disagreement says about the fix.

workshops.name: who-holds-the-gil
workshops.title: Who holds the GIL?
workshops.description: Profile a program with several threads using Tachyon. Why the default profile shows only a thread that is waiting, what -a adds, the flame graph's view of each thread, and GIL mode, on four threads of Python that take as long as one and four threads of hashing that do not.

workshops.name: the-price-of-an-exception
workshops.title: The price of an exception
workshops.description: Measure the time a program spends under an exception with Tachyon's exception mode, on a date parser that tries one format after another. What the mode counts, why raising is cheap and the handler is not, and the profile before and after the fix.
